# Dreams

Extensions of the idea, kept apart from the plan. Nothing here is researched.

Only a person moves a dream: `proto dream promote <id>` makes it a topic, and `proto dream drop <id> --why "..."` rules it out.

## Proposals

### You win by forgetting (d2)

What if forgetting a cache were the point, each lost acorn becoming a sapling, so the score is the forest you leave rather than the belly you fill

- Extends: The hoarding loop and what the player remembers
- Lens: the opposite
- Would take: an ending that shows spring growth, not survival statistics
- Scores: pull high, reach high, cost medium, fit high
- Verdict: proposed. It turns the plan's most dangerous mechanic — cache loss reading as bleak or as paperwork — into the scoring axis, and supplies a candidate answer to the still-open question of what the ending state is, all inside 2D, single-player, one forest, one winter.
- If adopted: The caching topic stops asking how retrieval should be tracked and starts asking which kinds of forgetting the player can read as consequence, while the winter arc has to establish a spring epilogue as the terminal state — so "reach the thaw alive" is no longer the win condition and an empty cache can no longer be defined as failure. The cozy/tense topic picks up a new open question: whether rewarding loss bleeds the tension out of scarcity, and what pressure replaces it.

### One night, one cache, five minutes (d4)

What if the whole thing were a single freezing night with one buried acorn, no art beyond shapes, judged only by whether playtesters lower their voices

- Extends: What the first slice contains and how it is judged
- Lens: the smallest version
- Would take: a weekend build and six strangers watched, not surveyed
- Scores: pull high, reach medium, cost low, fit high
- Verdict: proposed. It is the cheapest thing here that could actually move the stated goal, since it names a concrete build, a concrete observation, and a concrete population, and would be answerable before most of the horizon is spent; reach is only medium because the slice topic already contemplates an ugly prototype tested on strangers.
- If adopted: The first step becomes a single-night build in placeholder shapes, which pushes the solo art and audio pipeline question out of the opening weeks and removes full-run length and difficulty escalation as things that must be settled before anything exists. It forces the side-on-versus-top-down decision to be made quickly and provisionally rather than reasoned out first, and it requires naming the observable behaviour that counts as a yes before the build starts, since stated opinions stop being the evidence.

## Set aside

### A rehearsal for keeping something alive (d1)

What if the cozy tense pairing were offered to people nursing something fragile through a hard season, as a rehearsal of vigilance that ends in spring

- Extends: What makes it cozy and tense at once
- Lens: who else
- Would take: a difficulty dial that never mocks the player for choosing warmth
- Scores: pull low, reach medium, cost low, fit high
- Verdict: set-aside. Its only buildable take — a difficulty dial that never punishes choosing warmth — is already an open decision in the cozy/tense topic, so it re-frames who the game is for without settling anything the plan has not already put on the table.

### Ten winters, one lineage, one forest (d3)

What if one winter stretched into ten, played as a line of descendants, where the trees your grandparents forgot are the canopy you now climb and cache in

- Extends: Shape of one winter, start to finish
- Lens: ten times bigger
- Would take: a forest that persists and ages between runs
- Scores: pull medium, reach high, cost high, fit low
- Verdict: set-aside. It fights the stated one-forest-one-winter constraint head-on and adds cross-run persistence to a three-month solo budget, while the part worth keeping — forgotten caches becoming trees — is already carried by d2 at a fraction of the cost.

### The forest holds other real squirrels (d5)

What if the single player wall came down and your caches sat in a forest strangers also dig in, so being watched replaces being hunted

- Extends: Being small, cold and hunted in 2D
- Lens: remove the main constraint
- Would take: asynchronous presence: tracks, raided holes, nobody online at once
- Scores: pull medium, reach high, cost high, fit low
- Verdict: set-aside. Asynchronous presence is still other players, so it contradicts both the single-player constraint and the explicit multiplayer exclusion, and it adds a service to maintain that the horizon and the solo developer cannot absorb.

### Body condition as a bedside chart (d6)

What if hidden physiology were surfaced the way a bedside monitor does it, steady tones and a falling line, so the player reads the animal like a clinician

- Extends: How much real squirrel behaviour to simulate
- Lens: borrow from another field
- Would take: sound carrying the vitals so the screen stays a forest
- Scores: pull medium, reach medium, cost medium, fit medium
- Verdict: set-aside. It offers one concrete mechanism for a question the plan has left open in two topics at once — how body condition stays readable at a glance without covering the screen in meters — and is worth a look mainly so someone can rule on whether a clinical register fights the cozy side of the contract. A round proposes at most 3, and this was not among them.
